name: AD8676ARZ-REEL7
title: AD8676: dual precision op amp, 36 V, 2.8 nV/√Hz, rail-to-rail output
summary: A dual bipolar-supply op amp built for DC precision and low noise at once: 12 µV typical offset, 0.6 µV/°C maximum drift, 2 nA maximum bias current and 2.8 nV/√Hz at 1 kHz, with 10 MHz gain bandwidth. The outputs swing to within tens of millivolts of each rail; the input range is ±3.0 V on ±5 V supplies and ±12.5 V on ±15 V supplies. It runs from ±5 V to ±18 V and its figures are guaranteed from ±5 V to ±15 V over -40 °C to +125 °C. Suggested uses: precision instruments and medical equipment, PLL loop filters, the control loop of a laser diode, and amplifiers for strain gages and thermocouples. AD8676ARZ-REEL7 is an A-grade part in the 8-lead SOIC_N.

operation.text: Offset is screened in two grades. At 25 °C the B grade holds 50 µV in SOIC and 60 µV in MSOP, the A grade 100 µV in either; across -40 °C to +125 °C the limits are 160 µV (B) and 250 µV (A). All other limits are shared by both grades and both packages.

The output reaches close to both rails: within 50 mV typical at ±5 V into 10 kΩ, and the gap grows with load current (Figure 24). The input common-mode range does not include the rails; it is ±3.0 V on ±5 V supplies and ±12.5 V on ±15 V supplies.
Bring up both supplies before, or together with, any signal on the inputs. Where an input can be driven while the supplies are off, keep the current into it at 10 mA or less.
The voltage between the two inputs of one amplifier is rated to ±0.7 V at most; each input may swing to either supply.
At unity gain, small-signal overshoot climbs with load capacitance: about 12 % positive overshoot at 100 pF, near 40 % at 2 nF, about 48 % at 10 nF and above 55 % at 12 nF (Figure 17).
Driven into saturation at a gain of -100 with a 200 mV step, the output leaves the rail and settles back to its linear level in roughly 10 µs (Figures 18 and 19).
The AD8675 is the single-amplifier version.
